messages.content: What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?

message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) belong to the family **Felidae** in the order **Carnivora**, while zebras (Equus quagga) belong to the family **Equidae** in the order **Perissodactyla**.  
The last common ancestor of these two species is therefore the last common ancestor of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla – a member of the super‑order **Laurasiatheria**.

That ancestor was a placental mammal that lived roughly **70–80 million years ago** (late Cretaceous to early Paleogene). It was a small, generalized mammal that gave rise to the diverse lineages that eventually led to modern carnivores (cats, dogs, bears, etc.) and odd‑toed ungulates (horses, zebras, rhinoceroses, tapirs, etc.).
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. The common ancestor of lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) would be a common ancestor in the mammalian lineage. Both are mammals, but lions are felids (family Felidae), zebras are equids (family Equidae). They diverged from a common ancestor in the order Carnivora vs Perissodactyla? Actually lions are in order Carnivora, suborder Feliformia. Zebras are in order Perissodactyla (odd-toed ungulates). So their common ancestor would be a more distant mammalian ancestor, perhaps a placental mammal ancestor. The last common ancestor of all placental mammals is the eutherian ancestor. But maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species: that would be the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That would be the last common ancestor of the superorders Laurasiatheria? Actually Carnivora and Perissodactyla are both part of Laurasiatheria. So the last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla would be the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria. That ancestor would be a mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago. So the answer: the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is a Laurasiatherian mammal that lived about 70-80 million years ago. Or we can say the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is a mammal that lived in the late Cretaceous or early Paleogene. So answer accordingly.
